sections.html:
Greenwood County lies in the western Piedmont of South Carolina, with the city of Greenwood as seat and largest community. Hodges, Ninety Six, Troy and Ware Shoals are the other incorporated places. The 2020 Census counted 69,351 residents, nearly the same as 69,661 in 2010, and the 2025 estimate is 70,379.

Growth here has been slow and steady, so many houses stay with one family for decades and pass to heirs. An heir who does not plan to keep the property often finds a cash sale simpler than a listing. Lake Greenwood adds a layer of second homes, which are taxed differently from a primary residence (more on that below).

Three offices in the Greenwood County Courthouse, 528 Monument Street, deal with property tax. Each is open 7:45 to 5:30 Monday through Thursday and closed on Friday.

OfficeRoomPhoneWhat it handles
Assessor109(864) 942-8537Valuation and appeals
AuditorSuite 107(864) 942-8543Homestead and legal residence credit
Tax Collector101(864) 942-3142Payments, redemptions

One rule trips people up. An appeal must challenge value, use classification or ratio. Complaining that the bill is too big is not a valid appeal, so take that to the Assessor with a specific reason.

Greenwood County lets owners pay real estate tax in advance installments in February, April, June, August and October. Whatever remains is due on or before January 15 of the next year.

  • Pay at the counter, by mail, in the lobby drop box, or online through the county's payment vendor.
  • Cash, certified checks, money orders and major credit cards are all taken. Cards may carry a convenience fee.
  • Delinquent real estate tax cannot be paid with an out-of-state check.

Late charges come from state law, S.C. Code 12-45-180. That means 3 percent after January 15, a further 7 percent on February 2 and a further 5 percent on March 17. Ask the Tax Collector for the figure on your own bill.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and the school-tax credit
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is for an owner who is 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind. The applicant must hold fee simple title or a life estate in the primary residence and must have lived in South Carolina for a full calendar year as of December 31 of the prior tax year.

Legal residents also get a 4 percent homeowners credit on school operating taxes, so they pay only the school bond portion. Second homes, land and business property do not receive the credit. A lake cottage that is not your legal residence is therefore billed differently, and the Assessor can tell you how your parcel is classified.

If you sell or rent the home, or change who is on the deed, notify the Auditor. For a seller that means the exemption ends at the sale, and your buyer applies on their own.

Object in writing within 90 days of the mailing date when the notice raised value by $1,000 or more, as S.C. Code 12-60-2510 provides. The letter goes to the Assessor in Room 109.

Keep the letter to the point: name the parcel, say what value or classification you think is right, and give your reasons, whether that is a recent comparable sale or a condition problem the appraisal missed.

sections.h2: Farm land, rollback taxes and new construction
sections.html:
Agricultural-use classification calls for at least 5 acres in timber or 10 acres in crops, and pasture counts as crops. When the use changes, up to five years of taxes can come due. That is a real issue for anyone dividing a family tract before a sale, so ask the Assessor before you sign a contract.

Builders can seek an exemption on newly built single-family homes, and subdivision lots may qualify for a multiple lot discount. Both go through the Assessor.

sections.h2: Recording a deed and redeeming after a tax sale
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is in Room 114 of the courthouse, phone (864) 942-8612, open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. Documents delivered before 4 p.m. are recorded that day, later ones wait until the next day, and originals come back by mail 3 to 5 business days afterward.

The recording tax is $1.85 per $500 under Title 12, Chapter 24. State tax liens no longer get filed with county offices. They show up on the Department of Revenue's registry instead.

Redemptions after a tax sale go through Room 101 and are accepted as cash, certified check or money order only. Cards are not taken. Selling before the sale lets you skip that step altogether.

sections.h2: Selling a Greenwood County house that has tax or title issues
sections.html:
These are the steps most sellers follow:

  1. Ask the Tax Collector for the balance, including any advance installments already paid this year.
  2. Check with the Auditor whether a homestead exemption or school-tax credit is on the account, and tell that office about the sale.
  3. If the land has agricultural classification and you plan to split it, ask the Assessor what rollback tax could result.
  4. Pull the recorded deed from the Register of Deeds and confirm the seller's name matches. For an inherited home, the estate paperwork has to be in order before closing.

All three tax offices and the Register of Deeds share one building, so it is possible to cover every stop in a single trip, keeping in mind that the tax offices close on Fridays. A cash buyer purchasing as-is does not ask for a lender appraisal, and the closing date is yours to set around your own schedule.

faqs.q: What is the final payment deadline for Greenwood County property tax?
faqs.a: On or before January 15 of the year after the tax year. Advance installments are also available in February, April, June, August and October.

faqs.q: Is online payment available for Greenwood County taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Current and delinquent real, personal and mobile home taxes can be paid through the county's vendor, in person, by mail or in the lobby drop box. A card fee may apply.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the Greenwood County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Owners who are 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind and who meet the ownership and residency rules. Apply in person with the Auditor, and report any sale or rental.

faqs.q: How long can I contest a Greenwood County assessment?
faqs.a: Ninety days from the mailing of a notice that raised value by $1,000 or more. Send the written objection to the Assessor.

faqs.q: When are the Greenwood County tax offices open?
faqs.a: The Assessor, Auditor and Tax Collector keep 7:45 to 5:30 Monday through Thursday and close Friday. The Register of Deeds is open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday.
